name: The Ranch Malibu
who: 4- and 7-night residential retreat: 4-6 hours of coached daily hiking, plant-based meals, no phones, capped at 20-24 guests; from ~$1,200/night.
why: The benchmark hiking-based transformation retreat since 2010; the format every later hiking bootcamp on this list copies, with a long, quiet celebrity guest history.
takeaway: Book 4 or 7 nights of daily coached hiking, no phones — a hard reset, not a relaxing spa stay.

name: The Ranch Hudson Valley
who: East Coast sister of The Ranch Malibu, opened 2024: same 4- to 7-night guided-hiking, plant-based, digital-detox format an hour from NYC.
why: Extends The Ranch's proven hiking-retreat formula to the East Coast; fast becoming the default alternative for guests who can't get to Malibu.
takeaway: Book the same guided-hiking, digital-detox format as Ranch Malibu, just an hour from NYC — not a leisurely upstate trip.

name: The Body Camp
who: 7-, 14-night and multi-week bootcamp in a rustic Ibizan countryside villa: boxing, circuits, TRX, hikes, ice baths, plant-forward meals; returned to Ibiza for 2026-2027 after runs in Mallorca.
why: Entering its 11th year under coach Ricki Parcell, one of Europe's longest-running transformation bootcamp brands, with a large following built on visible client results.
takeaway: Book a multi-week bootcamp of boxing, circuits and ice baths under a named coach — transformation, not a villa holiday.

name: 38 Degrees North
who: 3- to 6-night boutique fitness retreats at five-star hotels (Aguas de Ibiza, Six Senses Ibiza), plus periodic London pop-ups; short-break format for fast fitness resets.
why: Running since 2012 with a steady stream of UK wellness-industry awards (2025-2026), known for pairing serious daily training blocks with luxury hotel settings.
takeaway: Book a short 3-to-6-night fitness reset at a luxury hotel — serious training blocks in a compressed break.

name: Wildfitness
who: Movement-and-nature retreats built around natural-movement training, beach and bush workouts, and deep-rest programming; runs seasonal retreats across the UK, Europe and its original Kenyan coast base.
why: One of the original 'ancestral fitness' retreat brands (25 years running), predating the natural-movement trend it helped popularize.
takeaway: Book a seasonal retreat of natural-movement training and deep rest — ancestral fitness, not a gym camp.

name: No1 Bootcamp
city: North Norfolk coast (year-round); also Ibiza, St Tropez, Marrakech, Portugal
who: Residential weight-loss and fitness camps, 15+ years running: 5-6 coached sessions a day, InBody body-composition scanning, chef-prepared meals; from ~£1,000/week.
why: The best-known year-round UK fat camp, now a 4-country operation off the original Norfolk site; regular UK press coverage of client transformations.
takeaway: Book this for heavily coached weight-loss with body-composition scanning — a serious fat camp, not a light fitness break.

name: Prestige Boot Camp
city: London, plus Portugal and Spain camps
who: Luxury weight-loss boot camp, established 2008, marketed as Europe's largest provider: intensive multi-session days aiming for 8-12 lbs lost per week.
why: Long-running, self-styled market leader in UK/European weight-loss boot camps, with a celebrity-fan page and steady Trustpilot review volume.
takeaway: Book this for aggressive, multi-session weight-loss days aiming for fast pound-per-week results — intensive, not gentle.

name: New You Boot Camp / New You Escapes
who: All-inclusive fitness holidays (rebranding under 'New You Escapes'), averaging ~6 hours of exercise a day; from ~£633/week.
why: One of the original 2000s-era UK boot-camp-holiday operators, still trading nearly two decades on, now spanning Spain and UK venues.
takeaway: Book this for around six hours of daily exercise at a budget weekly rate — volume-driven, not a boutique week.

name: Boot Camp Marbella
who: Year-round all-inclusive active holidays from a 4-star hotel base, training at Mike's Gym in Puerto Banus (ranked among Men's Health's top 10 world gyms) and on the Marbella Club beachfront.
why: Distinct from New You/Prestige, this operator's headline draw is training access to a genuinely elite gym facility rather than a generic outdoor circuit.
takeaway: Book this for access to a genuinely top-ranked gym, not a generic outdoor bootcamp circuit.

name: Northern Bootcamp
who: Family-run residential weight-loss boot camp at the Golden Hill Retreat on the Northumberland coast: boxing, circuits, dune runs, coasteering, plus a dedicated Military Prep course for armed-forces fitness tests.
why: A well-reviewed regional UK operator with a genuine niche — its Military Prep program specifically trains candidates for Royal Marine, Army, Navy and RAF fitness entry standards.
takeaway: Book the Military Prep course if you're training for armed-forces fitness tests — otherwise it's a regional boot camp.

name: Tiger Muay Thai
who: Stay-and-train Muay Thai/MMA camp with 150+ classes a week across fitness, yoga, BJJ, strength & conditioning and beach bootcamps; dorm rooms from ~6,000 baht/month up to bungalows.
why: The largest and most internationally recognized combat-sports training camp in the world, drawing fighters and fitness travelers from every continent year-round.
takeaway: Go if you want to train like a fighter — 150+ weekly classes suit committed combat-sports travelers, not casual gym-goers.

name: Unit 27
who: Original strength-and-conditioning box on Phuket's 'Fitness Street': CrossFit, Olympic lifting, team endurance events, women-only strength classes, military-influenced coaching.
why: Founded the Phuket fitness-tourism scene that Titan and others later joined; still runs the island's benchmark CrossFit Open and monthly throwdown competitions.
takeaway: Go for serious CrossFit and Olympic lifting with real competitions on the calendar — hardcore training, not a wellness retreat.

name: Titan Fitness Camp
who: All-inclusive outdoor fitness camp since 2013: boot camp circuits, obstacle courses, Hyrox training, cycling and yoga, plus a 'Work Train Travel' package for remote workers.
why: A well-established Fitness Street anchor with the strongest facility build-out on the strip — indoor gym, pool, sauna, ice baths — for its price point.
takeaway: Book this for Hyrox training and boot camp circuits with strong facilities — fitness camp, or work-and-train remote package.

name: Phuket Cleanse
who: All-inclusive detox-and-fitness retreat in a garden villa compound: bootcamps, Muay Thai, strength sessions and yoga paired with plant-based nutrition, infrared sauna and ice baths.
why: Fills the fitness-plus-detox niche in Phuket's crowded training-camp scene, with restorative facilities most pure bootcamps on the street don't offer.
takeaway: Book this for bootcamp and Muay Thai training alongside detox and ice baths — training plus recovery, together.

name: Mountain Trek Health Reset Retreat
who: 6- to 7-night hiking-based health reset in a glass-front timber lodge on Kootenay Lake: daily guided hikes, functional fitness, yoga, therapeutic massage, chef-prepared meals.
why: 35+ years and 10,000+ guests running Canada's most decorated hiking retreat, self-styled and widely cited as the #1 rated health retreat in Canada.
takeaway: Book 6-7 nights of daily guided hikes and functional fitness by the lake — active reset, not a lodge holiday.

name: The Ashram
who: Week-long residential program in the Santa Monica Mountains: sunrise yoga, daily hiking, fitness sessions, massage and plant-based meals; also runs international editions in Mallorca and Japan.
why: Founded more than 50 years ago and one of the earliest hiking-and-fitness retreats to attract a celebrity following (Cindy Crawford, Gwyneth Paltrow, Oprah have all attended).
takeaway: Book a week of sunrise yoga, daily hiking and coached fitness — a demanding program, not a relaxed retreat.

name: Bikini Bootcamp
who: Women-only weeklong retreat at Amansala: beach walks, morning yoga, fitness classes, sculpting sessions, yin yoga and spa services, running continuously since the early 2000s.
why: One of the pioneer women's fitness-retreat brands that helped put Tulum on the wellness-travel map, still running multiple dated retreats every year.
takeaway: Book a women-only week of beach walks, sculpting and yin yoga — a longstanding format, not co-ed intensity.

name: Live In Fitness
who: Residential weight-loss and body-transformation camp, 5-7 hours of daily coaching, customized meal plans and aftercare; from ~$3,490/week. Long-running Long Beach site also active; Hilton Head location closed.
why: 29 years trusted by pro athletes and TV networks (Dr. Phil, The Doctors), with a celebrity client list including Jessica Biel, Chris Paul and Angela Bassett.
takeaway: Book this for intensive coached weight-loss and body transformation with aftercare — a serious camp, not a light retreat.

name: Premier Fitness Camp
who: Adult weight-loss camp based at the Omni La Costa Resort: 4-5 hours of daily coached training at 3:1-4:1 client-to-coach ratios, behavioral-health and nutrition education; ~$6,000/week all-inclusive.
why: Leads its category on documented outcomes, citing UCSD-backed data on fat-loss-to-muscle-preservation ratios well above typical weight-loss-camp results.
takeaway: Book this for closely coached weight loss with documented outcomes data — a results-driven camp, not a casual fitness week.
